issue: Claude's decoder gives every text and thinking block in one message the same `message_id` (verified: decoding `tests/fixtures/claude/v1/healthy.jsonl` line 2 yields text and thinking, both `message-1`). The exact-ID key at model.py:576 therefore lets the thinking block replace the text, and "Working on the sanitized fixture." never reaches the panel. The test at tests/tui/test_activity_projection.py:83 (claude param) pins this kind-changing replacement as intended, and no test decodes a real Claude multi-block message. Fix: key on (kind, id), or add a block index at the decoder edge. If neither, record it as a deferred design gap.
reason: Confirmed decoded multi-block collision, but the explicit Projection contract requires a nonblank message_id to update its existing item regardless of kind. Design alternative 3 rejects new decoder identities. Changing to (kind,id) contradicts that contract. Defer this pre-existing design gap for a separate provider-edge design; retain HIGH severity and raw B1 fail. No finding is waived.

issue: Codex command detail is `command\noutput`, and `display_text` strips the `\n`, so the operator sees the command and its output run together ("printf exampleexample"). The new test asserts that string as the expected value (tests/tui/test_rework_activity.py:122), which treats an inaccurate render as intent. That conflicts with the PRD metric that tools "render accurate detail". Fix: turn line breaks into a visible separator before sanitizing, or record a deferral and stop asserting the fused text.
reason: Confirmed pre-existing newline concatenation. Projection and PRD require preservation of existing text sanitization; changing global display_text affects all panels. Defer a separately scoped separator design; retain the current regression assertion until behavior changes.

issue: The recovery fix still leaves one gap in the exit race. After `cleanup_run_records` removes run.json, the supervisor process stays alive until the interpreter exits. A poll in that gap gets `ended=False`, an idle observation with `run_id=None`, and `state=None`. Because that identity no longer matches the selected run, `_observe` closes the follower and clears the session cache. The next poll is terminal but has no `_session_id`, so the final frame loses lanes, activity and provider. I confirmed this with a probe: I ran `Selected.finish()`, forced `_run_observation.process_matches` to return True for one poll, and polled again. `assert_final_telemetry` then failed with `'unknown' == 'selected-provider'`. The new tests miss this because `finish()` waits for the process to exit fully. Fix: clear the cache only when `selected.ended` is true or the observation shows a different active run (`observation.run_id` is not None and differs). Missing metadata alone should not clear it.
reason: Confirmed cleanup-before-process-exit cache-loss edge. This predates and remains outside the activity projection contract; changing behavior when selected ownership metadata is absent needs a separate fail-closed observer contract covering replacement and malformed identities. Preserve the reported defect and probe; do not apply the suggested relaxed identity guard opportunistically. Correct consensus is Alice 1/3: Blake reported scope, Bob requested identity-guard coverage, not this defect.

It is needed for the full-suite exit gate and is documented in reports/00054-recovery-progress.md, but it has no PRD or design record of its own to trace it to.

issue: The lane window shows the first 20 lanes by insertion order, so the oldest-started lanes stay visible. Once a run has more than 20 lanes, the newest (running) lanes show up only in the "N lanes omitted" count. This repeats the R10 symptom ("hides recent work behind old … lanes") for lane-heavy runs. It is a literal reading of "existing order" and the design doc chose it, but it works against "keep the current activity visible".
reason: PRD explicitly says at most 20 lanes in their existing order. The design deliberately fixes this policy. Changing to newest lanes would contradict that explicit requirement; activity itself is newest-first.
